english: a great man can come from a hovel

terms.latin: Potest ex casā vir magnus exīre.
evidence: Sen. Ep. 66.3: Potest ex casā vir magnus exīre, potest et ex dēfōrmī humilīque corpusculō fōrmōsus animus ac magnus.
terms.comment: Literally “a great man can come out of a hut”: Seneca, of a friend whose fine mind lives in a frail body.

terms.latin: Exīre magnus vir ex tuguriō potest.
terms.comment: Traupman’s rewording of Seneca’s sentence, with tugurium for casa and the words in another order. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Seneca, Epistulae 66.3, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (12 November 2026).
